label: 2nd-3rd copy outputs in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the second and third copy steps (recall_idx 1 and 2, t = L+1 and L+2). recall_idx 2 holds about 75% of activation mass and recall_idx 1 about 22%. It never fires on original-phase steps, the <DEL> step, or the first output (recall_idx 0), and it is essentially silent from recall_idx 4 on. Rate and mass rise sharply with sequence length: L=9 holds 60% of mass, L=8 27%, and L<=5 almost none. Which tokens are involved also affects it: it is more likely and stronger when the third original token orig(2) is c, n or w (out_tok c has 9x lift; next_out c/n/w at recall 1). The top activations are at recall_idx 1 with orig(2) in {c, n, w}. This token preference is spread over many letters, so a token clause raises precision but costs a lot of recall. The position + length predicate catches about 84% of activation mass but has low precision (about 0.2): most long-sequence recall-1/2 steps stay inactive, depending on token content that I did not capture in the predicate.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: c, n, w, f, e, a; least: b, h, p, m) and the next token to output (most: c, n, w, f, q, a; least: i, -, h, m); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, t=10, recall_idx=1.
